name: Marimanindji
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sole sketch Tryon 1974 Daly Family Languages (PL C-32) read in full text via ANU repo: zero occurrences of stress/accent

sources.citation: Bicevskis, Katie. 2023. A grammatical description of Marri Ngarr. PhD thesis, University of Melbourne.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Marri Ngarr stress only; Marramaninjsji is mentioned once, for cognate density (54%).

sources.citation: Ford, Lysbeth. 1998. A description of the Emmi language of the Northern Territory of Australia. PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Emmi only; 'Marimanindji' appears once, on a tribal-territory map.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Marimanindji language' (accessed 2026-09-17); Glottolog 5.3 languoid mari1417; Wikidata Q10577424.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Wikipedia reproduces Tryon 1974's consonant chart and names Tryon 1974 as the primary description; nothing on stress. Glottolog lists only Tryon 1974 (grammar sketch, 10 pp.), Tryon 1970, Tryon 1968.

sources.citation: Green, Ian & Rachel Nordlinger (2022). The Daly Languages (Australia) website, Marramaninjsji page (id=16) and Resources / Typology pages.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that Tryon's word-list and sketch grammar (1968, 1970, 1974) provide 'the only published information thus far' and that 'Green (1990 ms; this website) builds on Tryon's preliminary account, with a core phonological and morphological overview, a learner's guide and an expanded wordlist' for the Kwombom Association; Ian Green's corpus = 6 h of recordings (PARADISEC IG4-001.006, IG8-009, IG8-012). The Green 1990 ms is not served on the site; the Typology page is 'still under construction'.

sources.citation: Nordlinger, Rachel. 2017. The languages of the Daly River region (Northern Australia). In Fortescue, Mithun & Evans (eds), The Oxford Handbook of Polysynthesis, 782-807. OUP (accepted manuscript).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing for this language; 'Marramaninjsji' appears only in the family table and as a language with no fluent speakers left.

sources.citation: Green, Ian. 1989. Marrithiyel: a language of the Daly River region of Australia's Northern Territory. PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Stress section 2.1.3 covers Marrithiyel (marr1257) only; Maramanandji is named three times as the Brinken sub-group sister on Marrithiyel's south side, with no data.

sources.citation: PHOIBLE 2.0, inventory ER 2637 'Marramaninyshi' (Round's Australian inventories), source given as Tryon 1974.
sources.note: Segment inventory (20 segments) only; no stress or tone information. https://phoible.org/inventories/view/2637

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1974. Daly family languages, Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-32. Canberra: ANU. Chapter 5 'Maramanandji', pp. 104-119 (5.2 Phonemes, p. 105 = PDF p. 123).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 5.2 is 'a tentative listing of the phonemes of Maramanandji' (consonant and vowel charts) with notes on stop voicing and the dental/alveolar contrast; 'the material collected in this language does not permit a definitive phonemic analysis'. Zero occurrences of stress/accent/syllable/suprasegmental in ch. 5; book-wide 'stress' hits are all 'it must be stressed'.

sources.citation: Tryon, D. T. 1968. The Daly River languages: a survey. In E. F. Aguas & D. T. Tryon, Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 3, 21-49. Pacific Linguistics A-14. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A14.21
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexicostatistical classification plus comparative wordlist of 24 Daly varieties; Maramanandji is no. 16 (Capell N.55). No phonological description of any language and no occurrence of 'stress'/'accent' in Tryon's paper (the volume's only Phonology section, p. 1, is Aguas' Gudandji paper).

sources.citation: Green, Ian. 1990 ms. Marramaninjsji: core phonological and morphological overview, learner's guide and expanded wordlist, prepared for the Kwombom Association (Daly River) with Ellen Sullivan, Lena Porter and Maudie Arriu.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only work described as containing a phonological overview of the language beyond Tryon's tentative phoneme list; Green's Marrithiyel thesis has a word-stress section, so his Marramaninjsji overview probably does too. Cited only on dalylanguages.org (view_language.php?id=16); not served there, not in Glottolog.
